# Create Spelling Performance Group Using Fitted Values from Quadratic to Plateau Model

[We deleted the section before showing a scatterplot between Age and Spelling Ability because who cares, we show the same thing below but with more information]

To address the concerns above, we can fit a quadratic to plateau model to model Spelling Ability as a function of Age. This will produce fitted values (aka the expected spelling score for each level of Age) that we can use to our advantage. We can take the difference of the observed value from the fitted value and then quantify this difference into quantiles. Those in the bottom 20% percentile will become the poor performance spellers while the rest will be the good performance spellers.

The advantage of this approach is that it basically categorizes poor spellers as individuals who performed poorly in comparison to individuals of a similar age. Also, the spelling ability scores were derived from a much larger sample, actually from the sample of all IDs that had spelling data. This is good because that sample was 661 subjects. Now while I am no IRT expert, I think this large of a sample size plus the fact that there were poor performers in the spelling task based on raw scores, justifies that standardized values, which represent distance from the mean performers, is still capturing true poor spellers. 


```{r Creating a spelling group using quadratic to plateau models}
# Load in the package
library(nlraa)
library(msm)

# run a quadratic to plateau regression
spell.nls <- nls(theta_good ~ SSquadp3xs(Age, a, b, jp), 
                 data = final_dat_sliced)

# Using predict2_nls() function to get SE for fitted values across level of Age
spell.nls.pred <- predict2_nls(spell.nls, newdata = NULL, interval = "confidence", level = 0.95)
final_dat_sliced$theta_good.fitted <- spell.nls.pred$Estimate

# Create the grouping variable based on subjects with less than - 1.5 SE from the model
final_dat_sliced <- final_dat_sliced %>%
  mutate(SpellDiscrepency = theta_good - theta_good.fitted,
         SpellThresh = quantile(SpellDiscrepency, 0.20), # 1-20% Percentile vs 20-100% percentile
         SpellThresh2 = quantile(SpellDiscrepency, 0.80),
         SpellGroup = ifelse(SpellDiscrepency <= SpellThresh, "Poor", "Good"),
         SpellGroup = factor(SpellGroup, levels = c("Poor", "Good")),
         SpellGroupExt = ifelse(SpellDiscrepency <= SpellThresh, "Poor",
                                ifelse(SpellDiscrepency >= SpellThresh2, "Very Good", "Average")),
         SpellGroupExt = factor(SpellGroupExt, levels = c("Poor", "Average","Very Good")))

# Add this information into the long final dataset
final_dat <- final_dat %>%
  left_join(select(final_dat_sliced, ID, SpellGroup, SpellGroupExt),
            by = "ID") %>%
  data.frame()

# View the number of participants in each group (original)
group.num <- xtabs(~SpellGroup, final_dat_sliced)
group.prop <- sapply(round(prop.table(xtabs(~SpellGroup, final_dat_sliced)) * 100,1), function(x) paste0(x,"%"))

# View the number of participants in each group (extremes)
group.num2 <- xtabs(~SpellGroupExt, final_dat_sliced)
group.prop2 <- sapply(round(prop.table(xtabs(~SpellGroupExt, final_dat_sliced)) * 100,1), function(x) paste0(x,"%"))


# Create a caption for the model
spl.coefs <- round(coef(spell.nls),2)
spll.caption <- paste0("Intercept = ", spl.coefs[1], "; slope = ", spl.coefs[2], "; join point = ", spl.coefs[3],
                       "; Good Spellers = ", group.num["Good"]," (",group.prop["Good"], ")",
                       "; Poor Spellers = ", group.num["Poor"]," (",group.prop["Poor"],")")

# Add the fitted values
final_dat_sliced %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = theta_good, color = SpellGroup)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .5, alpha = 0.6) +  # Added alpha for better visibility if overlapping
  geom_line(aes(y = theta_good.fitted), linewidth = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Generating Spelling Groups from EAP Scores After Accounting for Age",
    y = "Spelling Ability (EAP Scores)",
    caption = spll.caption,
    color = "Spelling Group") +
  theme_clean() 

# Create another version for very good vs poor spellers
final_dat_sliced %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = theta_good, color = SpellGroupExt)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .5, alpha = 0.6) +  # Added alpha for better visibility if overlapping
  geom_line(aes(y = theta_good.fitted), linewidth = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Generating Spelling Groups from EAP Scores After Accounting for Age\n(Extreme Groupings)",
    y = "Spelling Ability (EAP Scores)",
    caption = spll.caption,
    color = "Spelling Group") +
  theme_clean() 

```


# Age and Spelling Group Tabulation Table (Contingency Table)

Now that we have created a spelling group factor, let's see what the cell sample sizes are. We will bin people into age groups and then show within those bins, how many good and poor spellers there are. 



```{r spelling group by age contingency table}
# Create an Age group variable to see our sample size across age when turned into a factor
final_dat_sliced <- final_dat_sliced %>%
  mutate(Age_group = case_when(
    Age >= 15 & Age < 18 ~ "15-17",
    Age >= 18 & Age < 22 ~ "18-21",
    Age >= 22 & Age < 27 ~ "22-26",
    Age >= 27 & Age <= 38 ~ "27-38",
    TRUE ~ "ERROR"
  ))


# Use xtabs() to get a frequency table
xtabs_tb <- addmargins(xtabs(~Age_group + SpellGroup, final_dat_sliced), margin = 1)
xtabs_df <- as.data.frame.array(xtabs_tb)
xtabs_df$`Poor %` <- round(xtabs_df$Poor /  (xtabs_df$Good + xtabs_df$Poor),3) *100

# Some data cleaning
xtabs_df$age <- row.names(xtabs_df)
xtabs_df <- select(xtabs_df, age, Poor, Good, everything())
row.names(xtabs_df) <- NULL  

# Rename the variables
names(xtabs_df) <- c("Age Group", "Good", "Poor", "Poor %")

# Print out a nice table
xtabs_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Good and Poor Spellers by Age Group"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 13,
    heading.title.font.size = 18
  )

# Redundant table using the kbl() function instead
xtabs_df %>%
  kbl(caption = "<span style='color:black; font-size:16px; display:block; text-align:center;'>Number of Good and Poor Spellers by Age Groups</span>",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_paper(full_width = F)

```



# Visualizing Data Using Topographic Maps

We will no longer be removing subjects past this point, thus we can go back to our original long data, extract the IDs that made the cut, then use that information to plot topographic maps that can show us:
a) Effects of Age across the frequency bands
b) Effects of Spelling Performance across the frequency bands
c) Age x Spelling Performance interaction across the frequency bands 

```{r Visualizing topographic maps}
# Load in package
library(eegUtils)

# Extract the long information from the IDs that will be used for the analysis
data5L <- data4L %>%
  filter(ID %in% unique(final_dat$ID))

# Introduce Spelling Label into the data
data5L <- data5L %>%
  left_join(select(final_dat_sliced, ID, SpellGroup), by = "ID")

# Create a function to plot main topographic frequency band plots
topo_plot_fun1 <- function(data, FB) {
  # Filter the data by freq band then average across electrodes
  FB_data <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}}) %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  # Introduce electrode location
  plot_FB_data <- electrode_locations(FB_data)
  
  # Plot the data
  topoplot(plot_FB_data, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB))
 }

# Generate the plots for each topographical region
main_delta <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "delta")
main_theta <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "theta")
main_alpha1 <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "alpha1")
main_alpha2 <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "alpha2")
main_beta1  <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "beta1")
main_beta2  <- topo_plot_fun1(data5L, "beta2")

# Print all main plots side by side 
main_delta + main_theta + main_alpha1 # Slow waves
main_alpha2 + main_beta1 + main_beta2 # Fast waves


# Create a function to plot frequency band topographic plots by age group
topo_plot_fun2 <- function(data, FB) {
  # Filter the data by freq band then average across electrodes
  FB_data_young <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}},
           Age >= 15 & Age < 20) %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  FB_data_middle <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}},
           Age >= 20 & Age < 25) %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  FB_data_old <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}},
           Age >= 25 & Age < 38) %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  # Introduce electrode location
  FB_data_young <- electrode_locations(FB_data_young)
  FB_data_middle <- electrode_locations(FB_data_middle)
  FB_data_old <- electrode_locations(FB_data_old)
  
  # Plot the data
  plot1 <- topoplot(FB_data_young, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB, ": 15-19"))
  plot2 <- topoplot(FB_data_middle, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB, ": 20-24"))
  plot3 <- topoplot(FB_data_old, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB, ": 25-38"))
  plot1 + plot2 + plot3
}

# Create topographic plots grouped by sample ages
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "delta")
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "theta")
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "alpha1")
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "alpha2")
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "beta1")
topo_plot_fun2(data5L, "beta2")


# Create a function to plot frequency band topographic plots by Spelling Performance
topo_plot_fun3 <- function(data, FB) {
  # Filter the data by freq band then average across electrodes
  PoorSpellers <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}},
           SpellGroup == "Poor") %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  GoodSpellers <- data5L %>%
    filter(FB == {{FB}},
           SpellGroup == "Good") %>%
    group_by(channel) %>%
    summarise(power = mean(power, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(electrode = channel)
  
  # Introduce electrode location
  plot_PoorSpellers_data <- electrode_locations(PoorSpellers)
  plot_GoodSpellers_data <- electrode_locations(GoodSpellers)
  
  # Plot the data
  poor_plot <- topoplot(plot_PoorSpellers_data, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB,": Poor"))
  good_plot <- topoplot(plot_GoodSpellers_data, quantity = "power") + labs(title = paste0(FB,": Good"))
  poor_plot + good_plot
}

# Plot the frequency bands between good and poor spellers
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "delta")
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "theta")
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "alpha1")
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "alpha2")
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "beta1")
topo_plot_fun3(data5L, "beta2")
```



# Visualizing the Distribution of Absolute Power Within Topographies and in Relation to Age

The histograms of absolute power grouped for each topography are showing that the data is pretty skewed to the right. This is problematic because in order for us analyze our data we need to see a normal distribution to produce stable and reliable standard errors. Now this is not always the case, what really matters is the distribution of your errors, however this is a good shortcut to predict whether our errors will look normal or not.

In Whitford's paper, they also report that their distribution of absolute power for their sample was skewed also to the right. Since their analysis involved using regression, they needed their outcome distribution (absolute power) to look normal, thus they square root their data. 

Below we are doing something similar, we are plotting the distribution of absolute power in its original scale, after the values were transformed with the square root and a transformation of values using logarithm. We see below that our data looks best (normally distributed) when we use the log transformations. 

Additionally we are also showing the scatterplot between that transformation of the outcome (absolute power) and age. These descriptives give us a hint on whether or not we see that with age absolute power decreases, which theoretically is something we would expect.  

We can kinda see this with the slow wave, where with age the absolute power of the slow wave (0.5 - 7.5 Hz) decreases, however for alpha and beta we do not see this relationship.

```{r visualizing the relationship with age}
# Create a custom function for scatterplots
plot_scatr <- function(data, x, y) {
ggplot(data,aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}})) +
    geom_point(shape = 21,          # Creates circle with filling and border
             fill = "darkgrey",   # Inner fill color
             color = "black",     # Border color
             size = 1,            # Point size (adjust for thicker border)
             stroke = 1) +      # Border thickness (optional, default is 0.5)
  theme_clean() 
}

# Create a function to plot a frequency band by topography
plot_fb_top <- function(data, x, y, FB) {
data_filt <- data %>%
    filter(FB == !!FB) # To make it filter correctly

plot1 <- data_filt %>%
  plot_scatr({{x}}, {{y}}) +
  facet_wrap(~topography, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = paste("Frequency band:", FB))

plot2 <- data_filt %>%
  plot_hist({{y}}) +
  facet_wrap(~topography) +
  labs(title = paste("Distribution of:", FB))

# Print out both plots
plot1 + plot2
}

# Plot mean power regressed on age across topography for each FB
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "delta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "theta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "alpha1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "alpha2")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "beta1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, absolute_power, "beta2")

# Plot it but sqrt transformed
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "delta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "theta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "alpha1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "alpha2")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "beta1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, sqrt(absolute_power), "beta2")

# Plot it but log transformed
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "delta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "theta")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "alpha1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "alpha2")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "beta1")
plot_fb_top(final_dat, Age, log(absolute_power), "beta2")


```
# Creating Figure 1 for our paper

**Figure 1** is literally the information from above except made a little more prettier. We want to show how raw EEG power changes as a function of age. I think it makes the most sense to show the log transformed 

```{r Creating Figure 1 which is the relationship between EEG power and Age}
# Change the factor level of topography for plotting purposes
final_dat <- final_dat %>%
  mutate(topography = factor(topography, levels = c("frontal", "central","temporal", "parietal", "occipital")))

# Create some models to produce fitted values using predict
mod1 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "delta"))
mod2 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "theta"))
mod3 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "alpha1")) 
mod4 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "alpha2")) 
mod5 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "beta1"))
mod6 <- lm(log(absolute_power) ~ Age + I(Age^2) + topography, filter(final_dat, FB == "beta2"))

# Create fitted values
newdata <- expand_grid(
  Age = seq(14, 35, length.out = 100),
  topography = levels(final_dat$topography)) %>%
  mutate(topography = factor(topography, levels = levels(final_dat$topography)))


# Create a data frame of fitted values
fittedvals <- data.frame(
  Age = newdata$Age,
  topography = factor(newdata$topography, levels = levels(final_dat$topography)),
  fit1 = predict(mod1, newdata = newdata),
  fit2 = predict(mod2, newdata = newdata),
  fit3 = predict(mod3, newdata = newdata),
  fit4 = predict(mod4, newdata = newdata),
  fit5 = predict(mod5, newdata = newdata),
  fit6 = predict(mod6, newdata = newdata))


# Save the plots
```

### Simulate three potential outcomes for our data

```{r Simulating different outcomes we could find}
# a = intercept
# b = slope
# c = quadratic term (curvy bit)
# jp = join point = break point = critical concentration

qp <- function(x, a, b, jp) {
    c <- -0.5 * b / jp
    if_else(condition = x < jp,
            true  = a + (b * x) + (c * x * x),
            false = a + (b * jp) + (c * jp * jp))
}

# Create some fitted values
x <- 12:30
y1 <- qp(x, 28+16, -2-1.2, 25)
y2 <- qp(x, 36+16, -2-1.2, 25)
y3 <- qp(x, 36+20, -2-1.57, 29)
y4 <- qp(x, 28+18.5+3, -2-1.25, 26.5)
y5 <- qp(x, 28+18.5+4, -2-1.2, 27)

# Create a data frame
p_out <- data.frame(x = x, 
                    Good = y1,
                    Poor = y2)

# Create another dataframe
p_out2 <- data.frame(x = x, 
                    Good = y1,
                    Poor = y3)


# Create another data frame

                     Good = y4,
                     Poor = y5)

# Convert to long format
p_out_long <- p_out %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Good, Poor),
               names_to = "group",
               values_to = "y")

p_out_long2 <- p_out2 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols =  c(Good, Poor),
               names_to = "group",

p_out_long3 <- p_out3 %>%

h2 <- p_out_long %>%
```

### Fitting Best Quadratic to Plateau Model to Delta Frequency Band

Below we will be fitting the final model to answer our research question:

- Are there differences between good and poor spelling adults and does it show evidence for a maturational lag or a neurobiological deficit.
- Is the relationship above moderated by topographic regions? hemisphere? or both?

We will start by fitting the spelling factor first, then adding additional factors plus their interactions. Then we will do model comparison to identify which model best explains the data. 


```{r Fitting QTP on Delta data}
# Convert sex into a factor
final_dat <- final_dat %>%
  mutate(Sex = factor(Sex))

# Extracting datasets of interest
delta_dat <- filter(final_dat, FB == "delta")


# Create an outcome with the log transformed version of power for data within each frequency band
delta_dat <- mutate(delta_dat, log_absolute_delta_power = log(absolute_power))


##
###### Intercept = a
##

# Main effects only
delta_a_m1 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere + topography + SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ SpellGroup, xs ~ SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, 0, 
                                   xs = 28, 0),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))


# Spelling with Interactions for topography
delta_a_m2 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere + topography + SpellGroup +
                                       SpellGroup:hemisphere + SpellGroup:topography, 
                                     b ~ SpellGroup, xs ~ SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(3, rep(0, 12),
                                   b = -4, 0, 
                                   xs = 28, 0),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Spelling with Interactions for topography and hemisphere
delta_a_m3 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere * topography * SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ SpellGroup, xs ~ SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1) +  (1*1*4) + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, 0, 
                                   xs = 28, 0),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Model comparison
anova(delta_a_m1, delta_a_m2, delta_a_m3)


##
###### Slope = b
##


# Spelling Interaction with topography
delta_b_m1 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere * topography * SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ hemisphere + topography + SpellGroup + 
                                       SpellGroup:hemisphere + SpellGroup:topography, 
                                     xs ~ SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1) +  (1*1*4) + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, rep(0, 11), 
                                   xs = 28, 0),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Spelling Interaction with topography and hemisphere
delta_b_m2 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere * topography * SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ topography * hemisphere * SpellGroup, xs ~ SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1) +  (1*1*4) + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, rep(0, 4 + 1 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1)+ (1*1*4) + 1 - 1), 
                                   xs = 28, 0),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Model comparison
anova(delta_a_m3, delta_b_m1, delta_b_m2)

##
###### Join Point = C
##

# Spelling Interaction with topography
delta_c_m1 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere * topography * SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ topography * SpellGroup, xs ~ topography * SpellGroup),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1) +  (1*1*4) + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, rep(0, 4 + 1 + (1*4) + 1 - 1), 
                                   xs = 28, rep(0, 4 + 1 + (1*4) + 1 - 1)),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Spelling Interaction with topography and hemisphere
delta_c_m2 <-  nlme(log_absolute_delta_power ~ SSquadp3xs(Age_min_c, a, b, xs),
                        data = delta_dat,                               
                        fixed = list(a ~ Sex + hemisphere * topography * SpellGroup, 
                                     b ~ topography * SpellGroup, xs ~ topography * SpellGroup * hemisphere),
                        random = a ~ 1 | ID,
                        start = c(a = 3, rep(0, 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1) +  (1*1*4) + 1 - 1),
                                   b = -4, rep(0, 4 + 1 + (1*4) + 1 - 1), 
                                   xs = 28,  rep(0, 4 + 1 + 1 + (1*4) + (1*4) + (1*1)+ (1*1*4) + 1 - 1)),
                        control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Model comparison
anova(delta_b_m1, delta_c_m1, delta_c_m2)

# Best fitting model
paste0("Thus the best fitting mode is this (type III SS):")
anova(delta_b_m1, type = "marginal")

emmeans(delta_b_m1, ~ SpellGroup | topography, param = "a") %>% pairs()
emmeans(delta_b_m1, ~ topography | SpellGroup , param = "a") %>% pairs()
```

### Printing a Table for the Model Output

```{r Printing a table for the model ouput}
# Extract the fixed effects from the model.
slow_fix <- tidy(final_slow_mod) %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, ~round(., 3)) %>%
  select(-effect)

##
#### Correcting for multiple comparison
##

# Part1: get the index for topographic rows
topo_rows <- which(grepl("topography", slow_fix$term))

# Part2: split indices by parameter types
topo_pvals_a <- slow_fix$p.value[topo_rows[1:3]]
topo_pvals_b <- slow_fix$p.value[topo_rows[4:6]]

# Part 3: adjust the p-values using Holm-Bonferroni (stronger than Bonferroni)
topo_pvals_a_adj <- p.adjust(topo_pvals_a, method = "holm")
topo_pvals_b_adj <- p.adjust(topo_pvals_b, method = "holm") 

# IMPORTANT: Nothing really changed because 2 of the 3 p-values were already really small

# Test that it worked 
#p.adjust(c(0.02, 0.3, 0.01), method = "holm") %>% round(3)
#p.adjust(c(0.001, 0.19, 0.00001), method = "holm") %>% round(3)

# Introduced corrected-pvalues into the data
slow_fix$p.value[topo_rows[1:3]] <- topo_pvals_a_adj
slow_fix$p.value[topo_rows[4:6]] <- topo_pvals_b_adj


# Make the estimates prettier
slow_fix <- slow_fix %>%
    mutate(term = case_when(
        grepl("ecfrontal", term)          ~ "Frontal (Effect)",
        grepl("ecoccipital", term)        ~ "Occipital (Effect)",
        grepl("ectemporal", term)         ~ "Temporal (Effect)",
        grepl("a.Spell|b.Spell", term)          ~ "Poor Spellers (Effect)",
        grepl("a.(Intercept)", term, fixed = TRUE)  ~ "Good Spellers (Topography Grand Mean)",
        grepl("b.(Intercept)", term, fixed = TRUE)  ~ "Good Spellers (Topography Grand Mean)",
        grepl("xs.(Intercept)", term, fixed = TRUE) ~ "Good Spellers",
        grepl("xs.SpellGroup", term) ~ "Poor Spellers (Effect)",
    ))

# Change the names of the variables
names(slow_fix) <- c("Variable", "Estimate", "SE", "DF", "t", "p")

# Create a function for significance
p_function <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "<.001***",
         ifelse(p < .01, paste0(as.character(p),"**"),
                ifelse(p <.05, paste0(as.character(p),"*"), 
                       as.character(p))))
}

slow_fix$p <- p_function(slow_fix$p)

# Uncentered Title
slow_fix %>%
  kbl(caption = "<span style='color:black; font-size:16px;'>Slow Wave: Quadratic to Plateau Model Output</span>",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_paper(full_width = F) %>%
  pack_rows("Intercept (a)", 1, 5) %>%
  pack_rows("Instantaneous Slope (b)", 6, 10) %>%
  pack_rows("Join Point (xs)", 11, 12)

# Centered Title
slow_fix %>%
  kbl(caption = "<span style='color:black; font-size:16px; display:block; text-align:center;'>Slow Wave: Quadratic to Plateau Model Output</span>",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_paper(full_width = F) %>%
  pack_rows("Intercept", 1, 5) %>%
  pack_rows("Instantaneous Slope", 6, 10) %>%
  pack_rows("Join Point", 11, 12) %>%
  footnote("Topography effects display adjusted p-values using the Holm-Bonferroni method within each parameter section.")
  
```




### Results of 'Slow' absolute power as a function of age with Topography Between Spelling Group (Quadratic to Plateau Model)

The best fitting model was the one that still had slopes estimated for k-1 topography levels, so that is the one that we will be interpreting below. However, since this is our final model for the analysis, we will be interpreting the model not using the p-values directly from the output table, but the ones that we obtain using follow-up tests. This is so we can add adjustments to correct for multiple comparison. Additionally this will allow us to generate estimates for all levels of topography rather than just k-1 levels. Honestly, using **marginal effects** below, all previous models can essentially be ignored. Their reasoning for specification was to compare the results from these model back to them, to see if there are any weird discrepancies (ex: having a positive slope rather than negative or something crazy like that). 

Unfortunately, the omnibus test that we would typically use, aka the one from the Anova() function does not work here, so we will be ignoring that.

Okay so there is a lot of information down below, we will just make sense of the follow-up tests rather than the original model summary output. However, what is good about the model output is that it shows 1408 observations and 352 groups, which aligns with our dataset.

**Parameter a: The Intercept**

- Starting with **topography**, the estimated marginal means are showing the mean log absolute power for each level of topography when centered age is equal to 0 (age is 15 years). We see that all of them except for parietal are 2 log absolute power or larger. We can then do pairwise comparisons to test whether log absolute power differences between levels of topography. Looking at the p-values, we see that there are significant differences between frontal and parietal, temporal and occipital, temporal and parietal, and occipital and parietal. Essentially, from this we can see that in the parietal region, log absolute power tends to be lower overall compared to the other regions after adjusting for multiple comparisons (tukey)
- Next with **spelling group**, we can see the estimates between poor (2.03) and good (2.10) spellers. Instantly we can see that the values are very close to each other, not only that but **unexpectedly**, there is more log absolute power for good spellers than poor spellers. Next we investigate whether these means when centered age is 0 (age is 15 years) are significantly different from each other, and unsurprisingly they are not (p = 0.5844).

**Parameter b: The Slope**

- **Note**: The following slope estimates where all calculated from age centered being equal to 0 (age is 15 years). To do this, we created a reference grid that specified age centered being equal to 0, and then using that grid to obtain estimated slopes. This is important because failing to do this step would have produced either a) derivatives (slopes) averaged across all data points which include all age data points or b) an estimated slope at the sample mean of age centered. Those would have been **main effects**, but we don't really care for that since what we really want is the slope that corresponds with age centered being at 0.

- Starting with **topography**, we get the **simple slopes** of all levels of topography, where they are all negative and are all significant, indicating that with age log absolute power is decreasing, as we would expect. Next we use pairwise comparisons to see if the rate of change differs by topographical region. After controlling for multiple comparison using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, we found no differences in slope comparisons.
- Next with **spelling group**, we see that the simple slopes for poor spellers is -0.0691 and good spellers is -0.0766, which look similar, with the slope being slightly stronger for good spellers than poor spellers. Not surprisingly, the slope differences between the two were not significant.


**Parameter xs: The Join Point**

- We only modeled the join point using the **spell group** factor. We can see that the age for log absolute power plateau in poor spellers is 21.8 + 15 = 36.8 and in good spellers is 17.9 + 15 = 32.9. Again these numbers do not really make sense and the standard errors are large, especially for the poor spelling group with was 17.10 unlike the good spellers which was 5.52. How large these standard errors are really undermine the model entirely I would say. Regardles there was no significant difference in the join point between the two groups. 


```{r Results of the age with topography between spelling groups quadratic to plateau model}
# Print out the summary of the best fitting model
summary(final_slow_mod)

# Follow up tests on the intercepts (estimated marginal means)
(emm_top_a <- emmeans(final_slow_mod, pairwise ~ topography_ec, param = "a", infer = TRUE, adjust = "tukey"))
(emm_grp_a <- emmeans(final_slow_mod, pairwise ~ SpellGroup, param = "a", infer = TRUE, adjust = "tukey"))

# Create a dataset to get the slopes when Age is equal to 0
age_0_dat <- datagrid(Age_min_c = 0,
                      topography_ec = levels(slow_dat$topography_ec),
                      SpellGroup = levels(slow_dat$SpellGroup),
                      model = final_slow_mod)

# Follow up tests on the slopes
avg_slopes(final_slow_mod, variables = "Age_min_c", by = "topography_ec", newdata = age_0_dat)
avg_slopes(final_slow_mod, variables = "Age_min_c", by = "topography_ec", newdata = age_0_dat,  hypothesis = ~ pairwise) %>%
  hypotheses(multcomp = "holm")
avg_slopes(final_slow_mod, variables = "Age_min_c", by = "SpellGroup", newdata = age_0_dat)
avg_slopes(final_slow_mod, variables = "Age_min_c", by = "SpellGroup", newdata = age_0_dat,  hypothesis = ~ pairwise)

# Follow up tests on the 
(emm_grp_xs <- emmeans(final_slow_mod, pairwise ~ SpellGroup, param = "xs", infer = TRUE, adjust = "tukey"))
```
Just like before we can obtain fitted values of the model to create a scatterplot showing the relationships. We do this by using the `expand.grid()` function, where we can make different level combinations of all three predictors of interest: age centered, topography, and spell group. With this we can basically generate 100 observations for each level combination of the factors and confirm that this was correct using `xtabs()`.



```{r Visualizing the fitted values of the final model}
# Create a grid that has the predictor values we want for corresponding fitted values
newdat_final <- expand.grid(
  Age_min_c = seq(min(slow_dat$Age_min_c), max(slow_dat$Age_min_c), length.out = 100),
  topography_ec = levels(slow_dat$topography_ec),
  SpellGroup = levels(slow_dat$SpellGroup)
  
)

# Inspect the reference grid created
xtabs(~ SpellGroup + topography_ec , newdat_final)

# Add the predicted values back into the grid + adjust the age and relevel topography
newdat_final <- newdat_final %>%
  mutate(log_absolute_power = predict(final_slow_mod, newdata = newdat_final, level = 0),
         Age = Age_min_c + 15,
         topography = factor(topography_ec,
                             levels = c("frontal", "temporal", "parietal", "occipital")))

# Creating a pretty scatter plot
slow_dat %>%
  mutate(SpellGroup = factor(SpellGroup, levels = c("Poor", "Good"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = log_absolute_slow_power, color = SpellGroup, shape = SpellGroup)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = .7) +
  geom_line(data = newdat_final, aes(x = Age, y = log_absolute_power), size = 1) + 
  facet_wrap(~topography, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Fitted Values of Quadratic to Plateau Model Showcasing\n Log of Absolute Power Regressed onto Age by Topography\nBetween Spelling Groups for Slow Frequencies",
       y = "log of absolute power\n(slow frequencies)",
       color = "Spelling Groups",
       shape = "Spelling Groups") +
  theme_clean()

```

### Modeling the Error Structure


```{r Modeling the error structure}
# Our model already kinda has compound symmetric errors
# Do not run the following code, it produces the same output at the cost of an additional parameter
# final_slow_mod_cs <- update(final_slow_mod, correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~1 | ID))

# Produce the conditional residual correlations between topography
cond_resid <- final_slow_mod$residuals[,2]
cond_resid_matrix <- matrix(cond_resid, nrow = 352, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)
(top_res_cov <- round(cov(cond_resid_matrix), 3))
(top_res_cor <- round(cor(cond_resid_matrix), 3))

# Average pairwise correlations between topographies residuals
mean(top_res_cov[upper.tri(top_res_cov)])
mean(top_res_cor[upper.tri(top_res_cor)])

# Update the model with heterogenous variance
final_slow_mod_hcs <- update(final_slow_mod,
                          weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec))

# Creating a model with correlated residuals but homogenous variances
empty_lme_cor_res <- update(final_slow_mod,
                           correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID))

# Update to Unstructured Errors
final_slow_mod_un <- update(final_slow_mod,
                            weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec),
                            correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID))

# Model comparison on the modeleted error structures
anova(final_slow_mod, final_slow_mod_hcs, empty_lme_cor_res, final_slow_mod_un) # Unstructured wins

# View the residuals of this model - we can see the reduction in variances!
p_res_cs <- residuals(final_slow_mod, type = "normalize")# Now make the matrix and look at cov/cor
std_matrix_cs <- matrix(p_res_cs, nrow = 352 , ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)
round(cov(std_matrix_cs), 3)

p_res_hcs <- residuals(final_slow_mod_un, type = "normalize")# Now make the matrix and look at cov/cor
std_matrix_hcs <- matrix(p_res_hcs, nrow = 352 , ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)
round(cov(std_matrix_hcs), 3)

```

### Investigating differences in absolute between Spelling Groups in 'Alpha' and 'Beta' frequencies

Each model was fit using **maximum likelihood**, which makes model comparison comparable. We explicitly state maximum likelihood below since the default is restricted maximum likelihood. Regardless of approach to estimation, with technically REML being less biased, at a large enough sample size (which we have), the estimates between the models are essentially the same.

```{r Investigating differneces in absolute power for alpha and beta}
# Filter the data by frequency
alpha_dat <- final_dat %>%
  filter(FB == "alpha") %>%
  mutate(log_absolute_alpha_power = log(absolute_power))

beta_dat <- final_dat %>%
  filter(FB == "beta") %>%
  mutate(log_absolute_beta_power = log(absolute_power))

# Specify an alpha model with all variables of interest
a_mod1 <- lme(fixed = log_absolute_alpha_power ~ Age_min_c + topography_ec + SpellGroup,
              random = ~ 1|ID,
              data = alpha_dat, 
              method = "ML") 

# Specify another alpha model with a quadratic term
a_mod1_quad <- update(a_mod1, . ~. + I(Age_min_c^2))

# Model comparison to see if the quadratic produced better fit
anova(a_mod1, a_mod1_quad)

# Introduce alpha models with interactions because why not
a_mod2 <- update(a_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * SpellGroup)
a_mod3 <- update(a_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * topography_ec)
a_mod4 <- update(a_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * topography_ec * SpellGroup)

# Model comparison to see if any interaction led to better model fit
anova(a_mod1, a_mod2, a_mod3, a_mod4)


# Specify a beta model with all variables of interest
b_mod1 <- lme(fixed = log_absolute_beta_power ~ Age_min_c + topography_ec + SpellGroup,
              random = ~ 1|ID,
              data = beta_dat,
              method = "ML") 

# Specify another alpha model with a quadratic term
b_mod1_quad <- update(b_mod1, . ~. + I(Age_min_c^2))

# Model comparison to see if the quadratic produced better fit
anova(b_mod1, b_mod1_quad)

# Introduce beta models with interactions because why not
b_mod2 <- update(b_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * SpellGroup)
b_mod3 <- update(b_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * topography_ec)
b_mod4 <- update(b_mod1, . ~. + Age_min_c * topography_ec * SpellGroup)

# Model comparison to see if any interaction led to better model fit
anova(b_mod1, b_mod2, b_mod3, b_mod4)

```
### Printing out the best fitting models for higher frequencies


```{r Printing out the best fitting models for higher frequencies}
# Create a table with combined fixed effects from both models
alpha_beta_fix <- rbind(

tidy(a_mod1) %>%
  drop_na(p.value) %>%
  select(-group, -effect),

tidy(b_mod1) %>%
  drop_na(p.value) %>%
  select(-group, -effect)

) %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, ~round(., 3))

##
#### Correcting for multiple comparison
##

# Part1: get the index for topographic rows
topo_rows <- which(grepl("topography", alpha_beta_fix$term))

# Part2: split indices by parameter types
topo_pvals_a <- alpha_beta_fix$p.value[topo_rows[1:3]]
topo_pvals_b <- alpha_beta_fix$p.value[topo_rows[4:6]]

# Part 3: adjust the p-values using Holm-Bonferroni (stronger than Bonferroni)
topo_pvals_a_adj <- p.adjust(topo_pvals_a, method = "holm")
topo_pvals_b_adj <- p.adjust(topo_pvals_b, method = "holm") 

# IMPORTANT: Nothing really changed because 2 of the 3 p-values were already really small

# Test that it worked 
#p.adjust(c(0.02, 0.3, 0.01), method = "holm") %>% round(3)
#p.adjust(c(0.001, 0.19, 0.00001), method = "holm") %>% round(3)

# Introduced corrected-pvalues into the data
alpha_beta_fix$p.value[topo_rows[1:3]] <- topo_pvals_a_adj
alpha_beta_fix$p.value[topo_rows[4:6]] <- topo_pvals_b_adj

# Make the estimates prettier
alpha_beta_fix <- alpha_beta_fix %>%
    mutate(term = case_when(
        grepl("(Intercept)", term, fixed = TRUE) ~ "Intercept",
        grepl("Age_min_c", term) ~ "Age (centered at 14)",
        grepl("ecfrontal", term)          ~ "Frontal",
        grepl("ecoccipital", term)        ~ "Occipital",
        grepl("ectemporal", term)         ~ "Temporal",
        grepl("SpellGroupPoor", term)          ~ "Poor Spellers"
    ))


# Change the names of the variables
names(alpha_beta_fix) <- c("Variable", "Estimate", "SE", "DF", "t", "p")

# Make p-values prettier
alpha_beta_fix$p <- p_function(alpha_beta_fix$p)

# Centered Title
alpha_beta_fix %>%
  kbl(caption = "<span style='color:black; font-size:16px; display:block; text-align:center;'>Alpha and Beta Waves: Linear Model Output</span>",
      escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_paper(full_width = F) %>%
  pack_rows("Alpha Model", 1, 6) %>%
  pack_rows("Beta Model", 7, 12) %>%
  footnote("Topography effects display adjusted p-values using the Holm-Bonferroni method within each model.")

```

### Introducing Error Modeling for Both Models

```{r Introducing error modeling}
###
##### ALPHA
###

# Update the model with heterogenous variance
a_mod1_hcs <- update(a_mod1,
                     weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec))

# Creating a model with correlated residuals but homogenous variances
a_mod1_cor_res <- update(a_mod1,
                        correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID))

# Update to Unstructured Errors (Increased iterations to prevent convergence failure)
a_mod1_un <- update(a_mod1,
                   weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec),
                   correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID),
                   control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Model comparison on the modeled error structures
anova(a_mod1, a_mod1_hcs, a_mod1_cor_res, a_mod1_un) # Unstructured wins

###
##### BETA
###


# Update the model with heterogenous variance
b_mod1_hcs <- update(b_mod1,
                     weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec))

# Creating a model with correlated residuals but homogenous variances
b_mod1_cor_res <- update(b_mod1,
                        correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID))

# Update to Unstructured Errors
b_mod1_un <- update(b_mod1,
                    weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | topography_ec),
                    correlation = corSymm(form = ~1 | ID),
                    control = nlmeControl(msMaxIter = 2000))

# Model comparison on the modeled error structures
anova(b_mod1, b_mod1_hcs, b_mod1_cor_res, b_mod1_un) # Unstructured wins
```
